title: M1 Subscriptions and sending foundation: SES per site, double opt-in signup, subscriber records, one-click unsubscribe
description:
Outcome: a publication collects real, consented subscribers, and Distinctive Mark's existing signup forms go live (newsletter.signupEndpoint set; the subscribe page stops saying signups are not open). Worth shipping before any issue exists, because a list takes time to grow.

Scope:
- Per-site SES sending identity: sending subdomain, Easy DKIM, custom MAIL FROM, SPF, DMARC (Route 53 records), configuration set per site; SES production access request for papyrus-production (a support case, about a day).
- Bounce and complaint events (EventBridge) feed an automatic suppression list (SES account suppression plus our own per-site record).
- Alarms on per-site bounce and complaint rates that pause that site's sending before AWS thresholds (about 5% bounce, 0.1% complaint) can pause the shared account.
- Public signup endpoint: unauthenticated, rate-limited, bot challenge (e.g. Turnstile), double opt-in confirmation email. Choose its public path deliberately: /api/* on a /newsroom site already routes to the CMS app through the edge.
- Subscriber records: encrypted, separate from the content schema, lists and topic preferences, consent proof, status history; admin-only listing and export; erasure.
- One-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) and signed per-subscriber preference links, served by a small dynamic endpoint (the public site is static).
- Feature flag PAPYRUS_ENABLE_NEWSLETTERS; docs for enabling a site.

Done when: on distinctive-mark.com a reader subscribes, confirms by email, changes topics through a signed link, unsubscribes in one click from a real message, and an admin sees the subscriber count in the newsroom; a simulated bounce and complaint (SES mailbox simulator) are suppressed and alarmed.
